newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CBANK COULD DAMPEN GDP GROWTH - SUSR HEAD.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CBANK COULD DAMPEN GDP GROWTH - SUSR HEAD.

text.p: The head Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) on Wednesday downgraded the bureau's gross domestic product forecast for 1996 to 6.4 to 7.0 percent from its previous forecast of 7.1 percent growth.

The bureau released a statement listing only its revised forecast of 7.0 percent growth, but SUSR Chairman Stefan Condik warned the country's central bank could further dampen growth if it adopted further restrictive policy measures.

"We forecast real GDP growth within a 6.4-7.0 percent interval by the end of the year, but this will not hold if the central bank starts acting as if the economy was overheating," Condik told a news conference.
The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) implemented a series of measures in July aiming to tighten the money supply.
The moves included hikes in the Lombard last-resort lending facility and minimum reserve requirements for banks, which boosted the interbank money market rates to a 13-14 percent.
"In our opinion raising loan interest (rates) means that the current growth is further to be tightened or propelled pending on the NBS policy," Condik said.
Condik said SUSR's GDP forecast was also based on a bureau survey of expectations by major exporters and producers.
"It seems that these (restricitve) central bank measures will remain in force as long as the problem of bad loan portfolios of Slovak banks is not solved," Condik added.
Condik said the latest inflation figures showed that the economy had not reached the stage of overheating.
"We still could have waited, the inflation developments favoured that".
Still the lowest in eastern Europe, Slovak inflation measured by consumer price index rose 5.6 percent year-on-year in August, after a 5.5 percent increase in July.
However, Slovakia's key money supply measure, M2, rose 21.0 percent year-on-year in July, compared to a full-year target of an expansion of 11.6 percent year-on-year.
